submission.reason: Exploration of data/explore.csv showed that hospital site strongly predicts recovery_score (H3/H4 much higher than H1), but no candidate exposure had a significant within-site (hospital-adjusted) association with recovery_score. The full OLS with all ten exposures plus site indicators left every exposure non-significant (all p>0.25), and within-site centered correlations were all small and non-significant. The most consistent candidate, crp_level (negative within-site correlation in all four sites, largest coefficient magnitude), was tested with the pre-registered confirmatory OLS on held-out data: estimate -0.070 (SE 0.117), p = 0.552, not significant at alpha=0.05. The confirmatory test therefore did not confirm a direct effect for any exposure.

df = pd.read_csv('data/explore.csv')

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
from scipy import stats
df = pd.read_csv('data/explore.csv')
exposures = ['vitamin_d','sleep_hours','steps_k','bmi','crp_level','dose_mg','age_decades','sodium_mmol','hdl','stress_index']
d = df.dropna(subset=exposures+['recovery_score']).copy()
# within-site centered regression (equivalent to site FE)
for e in exposures:
    xs=[]; ys=[]
    for h,g in d.groupby('hospital'):
        xs.append(g[e].values-g[e].mean()); ys.append(g['recovery_score'].values-g['recovery_score'].mean())
    x=np.concatenate(xs); y=np.concatenate(ys)
    r,p=stats.pearsonr(x,y)
    # per-site sign
    signs=[np.sign(g[e].corr(g['recovery_score'])) for h,g in d.groupby('hospital')]
    print(f"{e:14s} within_r={r:+.3f} p={p:.4f} signs={signs}")

    print(f"{e:14s} within_r={r:+.3f} p={p:.4f} signs={signs}")
"}
